transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me your name and what brings you in today?

Hi. I'm Brenda. Um, I came in today because... well, most days I just feel like I’m sitting at the bottom of a dark hole. 

Which is kind of ironic, I guess, because I do HVAC maintenance and repair for a living, so I'm literally crawling around in dark spaces all the time. Just the other day I was under this house over on Maple Street, and the ductwork was a complete disaster. Raccoons had gotten in and tore the insulation to shreds. You wouldn't believe the mess. And the homeowner was this guy who just kept hovering by the access door, trying to talk to me about his golf swing while I'm elbow-deep in fiberglass and raccoon droppings. People are just so oblivious sometimes, you know? They don't pay attention to what's going on around them. 

But, um... anyway. Even when I'm not at work... like, even when I’m around people I know, my friends or whatever, I just can’t shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. It's just always there.
How long have you been feeling this way — this heavy, hopeless feeling that you mentioned?

Um, it’s been... gosh, about a year and two months now. Yeah, right around fourteen months. Everything really started unraveling ever since this fall I had at a job site that left me with a pretty bad back injury. 

I was working on this ancient rooftop unit, and the access ladder was just completely rusted out. Which, honestly, is a huge safety violation, but my boss at the time—this guy named Stan—he was always cutting corners. Stan would squeeze a dime until Roosevelt screamed, I swear. He actually tried to make me pay for my own work boots once, even though it's clearly stated in our contract that the company provides the safety gear. I had to get the rep involved and everything. It was a whole big ordeal, just over a pair of steel-toed boots. And the boots they finally gave me weren't even the right brand, they were those cheap knock-offs that give you blisters the size of quarters if you wear them for more than an hour on the concrete. I tried putting those gel inserts in them, but it didn't really help, it just made the toe box too tight... 

Wait, I'm sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right. The heavy feeling. Yeah, it's been there for about a year and two months, ever since that fall.
Brenda, have you noticed a decrease in your interest or pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy, like hobbies or spending time with friends?

Yeah... yeah, I really have. I used to be doing something all the time. I loved hiking up at the state park, and I did some watercolor painting... plus I'd always be down at the community makerspace tinkering with things. Honestly, I even used to get a kick out of figuring out a really tricky HVAC install at work. Like when you have to route the ductwork through a crawlspace that wasn't built to code in the first place. 

I remember this one house, built back in the 1920s, and the original owner had done all the plumbing himself. It was a complete labyrinth of galvanized pipes just going nowhere. I had to basically invent a new way to hang the return lines without hitting any of his crazy pipe maze. And the homeowner's cat—this massive orange tabby named Meatball—just sat there on a joist watching me the whole time, judging my every move. Meatball actually swatted at my flashlight once and knocked it right into a puddle of what I really hope was just condensation. I had to buy a new flashlight after that. I got one of those heavy-duty tactical ones that you can drop from a roof, you know? They have them at the hardware store by the register. 

But... um, anyway. Now? Now I just don't care. I'll look at my paints or my tools and I just stare at them. My friends will call to see if I want to go to the makerspace or go on a hike, and I just ignore the phone. It just... none of it feels worth the effort to even start.

Brenda, have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgety and restless lately? Like, has your body ever felt like it was moving through molasses, or like you couldn't sit still?

Molasses... yeah, or underwater. That's exactly what it feels like. Everything I do is just so slow now. Like, just getting from the couch to the kitchen takes me longer than it should. 

Which reminds me, my refrigerator has been making this awful rattling noise lately. I know exactly what it is, too, it’s the evaporator fan motor. The bearings are starting to go out. I should just order the part, it’s only like thirty bucks on this wholesale supply website I use, but the shipping delays right now are just ridiculous. We had a client at work waiting three weeks for a standard blower motor. Three weeks! The lady was calling the shop every single day, just screaming at our dispatcher, Patty. And Patty doesn't deserve that, she's the sweetest lady. She brings in these amazing blueberry muffins on Fridays. Made from scratch. She says it's her grandmother's recipe, but I swear she puts a little lemon zest in the batter, it gives it this little kick that you don't expect from a regular muffin... 

Um, I'm sorry, my brain just kind of wanders off. But yeah, people keep asking me if I’m okay lately. Because I really do just move like I’m underwater. Even just... answering a simple question takes me so much longer than it used to. Everything is just slow.
Brenda, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately — like eating much less than usual or losing weight without trying?

Yeah, my eating is just... it's all over the place right now. I'll go almost the whole day just drinking coffee because the thought of food just completely turns my stomach. 

I buy that bulk coffee from the warehouse club, you know? The big three-pound bags of the French roast. It's actually not a bad deal, but the last time I went, they had rearranged the entire store. Why do they do that? You get used to the aisles, you know exactly where the paper towels and the coffee are, and then bam, suddenly the coffee is over by the automotive supplies. I spent twenty minutes just wandering around looking for it. And they had this display of windshield wipers right next to it, which reminded me that I need to change the wipers on my truck. I usually get the silicone ones because they last longer, especially with the harsh winters we get here. The cheap rubber ones just crack and streak after one season, and there's nothing worse than driving home in the sleet and not being able to see out of your windshield. It's so dangerous. My dad always used to say, "Never skimp on tires or wipers, Brenda." He was a mechanic for thirty years, so he knew what he was talking about. He worked at this little independent shop down on 4th Street... 

Wait, what was the question? Oh, right, my weight. Yeah, so I just drink coffee all day, and then late at night, I just kind of pick at whatever's in the cabinet. I'm not even really tasting it, I'm just eating crackers or whatever I can find. So yeah, my appetite is definitely messed up.
Brenda, have you been having any trouble with your sleep lately — like difficulty falling asleep, waking up during the night, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, sleep is... it's a mess. I either lie awake for hours, just staring at the ceiling. My lower back will be throbbing from work, and my brain just won't shut up about all the bills I have to pay. 

Speaking of bills, the utility company just raised their rates again. Did you see that? It was on the local news. They sent this little flyer in the mail with the last statement, trying to explain why it’s necessary for "grid modernization," but it's just ridiculous. It's going up like fifteen percent. I was talking to my neighbor, Gary, about it. Gary is retired, he used to work for the postal service, so he's on a fixed income, and he is just furious. He said he's going to start putting solar panels on his roof, but his roof is so old, I told him he's going to have to replace the shingles first. You can't just bolt heavy brackets into twenty-year-old asphalt shingles, you'll get leaks the first time it rains. I offered to go up in his attic and check his rafters, because in those older houses, sometimes the framing is just 2x4s spaced too far apart, and that won't hold the snow load plus the panels... 

Um, but yeah. Sleep. When I'm not lying awake worrying about money, the other thing that happens is I'll finally crash and sleep half the day away. But even when I sleep for twelve hours, I wake up feeling completely exhausted, like I never rested at all.
Brenda, have you ever felt like life isn’t worth living, or had thoughts about harming yourself?

Yeah... I have. It's hard to talk about, but... yeah. I've been having these thoughts lately that everyone would just be better off if I didn't wake up. 

I mean, my sister has been calling me a lot lately, checking in. She lives over in Ohio, near Dayton. Have you ever been to Dayton? They have that huge aviation museum there, the Air Force one. We went when we were kids, and they have all these old planes just hanging from the ceiling. It's actually incredible how they suspend them like that. The cable rigging they must use... I was looking at the structural supports when we went back a few years ago, and they must have reinforced the trusses specifically for that load. You can't just hang a B-52 from a standard steel beam, you need serious tensile strength. I was trying to explain that to my nephew, but he was just interested in the gift shop. Kids are like that, you know? They just want the little plastic planes that break the second you take them out of the package. I bought him this die-cast one instead, much better quality. Die-cast metal will last forever if you don't leave it out in the rain...

But, um... what was I saying? Oh. The thoughts. Yeah, when the pain in my back gets really bad and the money worries just keep piling up, I catch myself thinking about ending it. Just... making it all stop. It scares me when my brain goes there, it really does, but the thoughts are definitely there.
